strings.d1.s0.name: Peak Tram
strings.d1.s0.tips: The first trams at 07:30 have no queue. It takes 8 minutes to reach Victoria Peak; around 88 HKD return.
strings.d1.s1.name: Victoria Peak Sky Terrace 428
strings.d1.s1.tips: The terrace at the summit has 360° views of the harbour, and the morning haze clears.
strings.d1.s2.name: Peak Circle Walk
strings.d1.s2.tips: A flat 3.5 km walk around the summit, shaded and scenic.
strings.d1.s3.name: Tim Ho Wan Central
strings.d1.s3.tips: The world's cheapest Michelin-starred dim sum. Don't miss the BBQ pork buns (char siu bao).
strings.d1.s4.name: Central-Mid-Levels Escalator
strings.d1.s4.tips: The world's longest outdoor covered escalator system, leading up to SoHo and Tai Kwun.
strings.d1.b0.name: Lan Fong Yuen
strings.d1.b0.tips: A cha chaan teng (Hong Kong tea café) since 1952. Try the milk tea and the pork chop sandwich.
strings.d1.b1.name: Tai Kwun
strings.d1.b1.tips: A former police station and prison, now a free cultural centre.
strings.d2.s0.name: Star Ferry Central Pier
strings.d2.s0.tips: The legendary 8-minute ferry from Central to Tsim Sha Tsui. It costs 5 HKD with an Octopus card.
strings.d2.s1.name: Tsim Sha Tsui Promenade
strings.d2.s1.tips: The Avenue of Stars and harbour views. Good for morning photos.
strings.d2.s2.name: Hong Kong Museum of Art
strings.d2.s2.tips: A harbourfront art museum with free entry, showing Chinese calligraphy and contemporary art.
strings.d2.s3.name: Mak's Noodle Jordan
strings.d2.s3.tips: A wonton noodle classic. The bowls are small, so order two.
strings.d2.s4.name: Temple Street Night Market
strings.d2.s4.tips: Fortune tellers, street food and cheap goods. It comes alive after 18:00; try the claypot rice.
strings.d2.b0.name: Australia Dairy Company
strings.d2.b0.tips: Egg sandwiches on toast and steamed milk pudding. The queue moves fast.
strings.d2.b1.name: Kowloon Park
strings.d2.b1.tips: A park in Tsim Sha Tsui with flamingos. A swap for the museum.
strings.d3.s0.name: Ngong Ping 360 Cable Car
strings.d3.s0.tips: A 25-minute cable car ride from Tung Chung (around 300 HKD return; glass-bottom cabins cost extra), with views of sea and mountains.
strings.d3.s1.name: Tian Tan Buddha
strings.d3.s1.tips: A 34 m bronze Buddha. Climb the 268 steps for views over Lantau.
strings.d3.s2.name: Po Lin Monastery
strings.d3.s2.tips: The monastery at the foot of the Buddha. Vegetarian meal tickets are sold here.
strings.d3.s3.name: Po Lin Vegetarian Restaurant
strings.d3.s3.tips: The monastery's vegetarian kitchen: simple and good.
strings.d3.s4.name: Tai O Fishing Village
strings.d3.s4.tips: A village of stilt houses. A boat tour (with a chance of pink dolphins) costs 30 HKD, and there is a dried fish market.
strings.d3.b0.name: Tai O Dried Seafood Market
strings.d3.b0.tips: Grilled seafood in Tai O. A swap for the monastery.
strings.d3.b1.name: Cheung Sha Beach
strings.d3.b1.tips: Lantau's long beach, good for swimming in summer.
strings.d4.theme: Mong Kok and Sham Shui Po
strings.d4.s0.name: Chi Lin Nunnery
strings.d4.s0.tips: A Tang-style wooden nunnery built without nails, with lotus ponds.
strings.d4.s1.name: Nan Lian Garden
strings.d4.s1.tips: A Chinese garden opposite the nunnery, with a golden pagoda.
strings.d4.s2.name: Wong Tai Sin Temple
strings.d4.s2.tips: Fortune sticks (kau cim) and incense. It is Hong Kong's busiest temple.
strings.d4.s3.name: Kwan Kee Bamboo Noodle
strings.d4.s3.tips: In Sham Shui Po, noodles kneaded with a bamboo pole. A legend.
strings.d4.s4.name: Apliu Street, Sham Shui Po
strings.d4.s4.tips: An electronics and fabric market in Hong Kong's most local neighbourhood, with street food.
strings.d4.b0.name: Tim Ho Wan Sham Shui Po
strings.d4.b0.tips: The original Tim Ho Wan branch.
strings.d4.b1.name: Ladies' Market Mong Kok
strings.d5.s0.name: Repulse Bay Beach
strings.d5.s0.tips: A sandy beach on the south of the island. Sun loungers are free, there are showers, and mornings are quiet.
strings.d5.s1.name: Stanley Market
strings.d5.s1.tips: A market in a seaside town, selling silk and souvenirs.
strings.d5.s2.name: The Boathouse Stanley
strings.d5.s2.tips: Seafood on the Stanley waterfront, with a terrace.
strings.d5.s3.name: Stanley Promenade
strings.d5.s3.tips: Murray House and the waterfront. Stop for coffee.
strings.d5.s4.name: Shek O Beach
strings.d5.s4.tips: A village beach, good for a sunset swim.
strings.d5.b0.name: Stanley Plaza Food Court
strings.d5.b1.name: Deep Water Bay
strings.d5.b1.tips: A quieter cove next to Repulse Bay.
strings.d6.s0.name: Yung Shue Wan Lamma
strings.d6.s0.tips: A 30-minute ferry from Central. A car-free island village with cafés.
strings.d6.s1.name: Lamma Family Trail
strings.d6.s1.tips: A 1.5-hour coastal walk from Yung Shue Wan to Sok Kwu Wan, with a stop at Hung Shing Yeh beach.
strings.d6.s2.name: Hung Shing Yeh Beach
strings.d6.s2.tips: Lamma's swimming beach, with showers and a snack bar.
strings.d6.s3.name: Rainbow Seafood Lamma
strings.d6.s3.tips: Seafood in Sok Kwu Wan, with a free ferry back to Central.
strings.d6.s4.name: Sok Kwu Wan Pier
strings.d6.s4.tips: Fish farms and the return ferry.
strings.d6.b0.name: Lamma Bookworm Cafe
strings.d6.b1.name: Cheung Chau Island
strings.d6.b1.tips: An alternative island, good for cycling and beaches.
strings.d7.s0.name: Hong Kong Park
strings.d7.s0.tips: A park among the skyscrapers, with an aviary and a lake.
strings.d7.s1.name: Ding Ding Tram Line
strings.d7.s1.tips: Ride the historic double-decker tram to Wan Chai. Take a front seat upstairs; the fare is 3 HKD.
strings.d7.s2.name: Kam's Roast Goose Wan Chai
strings.d7.s2.tips: Michelin-starred roast goose for a farewell lunch. Expect a 30-minute queue.
strings.d7.s3.name: Airport Express Hong Kong Station
strings.d7.s3.tips: The airport train takes 24 minutes, with in-town check-in.
strings.d7.b0.name: Joy Hing Roasted Meat
strings.d7.b0.tips: Cheap char siu in Wan Chai.
strings.d7.b1.name: Blue House Wan Chai
strings.d7.b1.tips: A historic blue building and neighbourhood museum. A swap for the tram.
strings.note0: An Octopus Card works for everything (MTR, trams, ferries, shops); buy one at the airport. The Airport Express takes 24 minutes.
strings.note1: Summers are humid at 33°C, and typhoon warnings are possible (everything closes at Signal 8). Sightsee in the morning and head to malls or museums in the afternoon.
strings.note2: Dim sum is eaten in the morning and at lunchtime. Queues are normal at cheap Michelin-listed places like Tim Ho Wan and Kam's Roast Goose.
strings.note3: Tipping is not expected, as a 10% service charge is added. Cash is still common; small restaurants don't take cards.
strings.note4: The Star Ferry and the Peak Tram are Hong Kong rituals. Go up to the Peak at 08:00, and return at 19:00 for the evening lights.
strings.note5: Bring your passport for Macau. Ferries to Lamma and Cheung Chau leave from Central Piers 4 and 5.
strings.transit.name: Octopus Card
strings.transit.why_chosen: It works on the MTR, trams, buses, the Star Ferry and in shops, so it is useful everywhere in Hong Kong.
